description: pkix-chain/tests/hostname_corpus.rs uses `Rfc5280Profile` for verify_tls_server tests. pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:720 rustdoc says 'typically BasicTlsProfile or WebPkiProfile' which would REQUIRE id-kp-serverAuth. Rfc5280Profile is permissive — no EKU enforcement. The corpus tests therefore validate the SAN-binding mechanics but DO NOT verify that a non-serverAuth cert (e.g., a code-signing cert that happens to carry a DNS SAN) is correctly rejected. This is a coverage gap: a caller using BasicTlsProfile with verify_tls_server expects 'TLS server' semantics, but the test suite never confirms that the wrapper enforces the EKU. Fix: parallel run of one or two corpus cases under BasicTlsProfile, with a fixture that has a DNS SAN but lacks id-kp-serverAuth. Confirms the EKU enforcement composes with SAN matching. (Note: test case #25 'basictls_profile_exact_match' uses BasicTls but only on a cert that has the correct EKU — does not exercise the rejection path.)
title: Hostname/mailbox corpus tests use Rfc5280Profile, not the profile rustdoc recommends
